feed.title: The Ringshadow blog
feed.subtitle: How Ringshadow is being built, as it happens.

entry.title: The away report: what your world did without you
entry.summary: The server keeps a ledger for every pilot off line, from its own bookkeeping and never invented, and reads it back on the home screen, in a toast, on the radio and in the Journal. Plus the goals that now lead on from a Foundry.

entry.title: A Citadel in every region
entry.summary: The realm limit is now one Citadel a region instead of one a realm, and each is a full home: unload with the realm's tax, respawn at the nearest, respec, the Citadel screen on the one wallet, four corner turrets. Milestone 10's first merge.

entry.title: The day the sky got too heavy
entry.summary: A Prospector that seemed to die and a world that came back empty: neither happened. Sixty-one starfalls rode in every part of every snapshot, so no snapshot arrived whole. The save was intact all along; the fix is what a pilot is told.

entry.title: The crossing hitch: three wrong checks and five real causes
entry.summary: The seamless region crossing hitched five frames after the change. The checks that watched it were wrong three ways and the spike had five causes, all fixed: 31 to 37 ms down to about 14. And why 2 of 35 packaged launches died.

entry.title: Realm projects: what the tax is for
entry.summary: The realm wallet now funds four realm-wide projects, a world day each: the Beacon halves Dropship fares, the Relay widens every pilot's night sight, the Armoury lifts every turret a mark, the Dock Crew doubles the mercenaries. M9 is closed; M10 is planned.

entry.title: The packaged build, measured: a 1,547 ms stall down to 42
entry.summary: The online mode packaged as a Mac app and measured in hidden runs, not shipped: it starts four times sooner than the editor, draws as fast, and the first Dropship call's stall had three causes, all fixed.

entry.title: Build anywhere in the canyon
entry.summary: No more build spots: place any building anywhere standable in a canyon, packed as tight as you like. Walkers route round what they can and bite through what walls them off; two cells funnel, one cell walls.

entry.title: The siege has a sound
entry.summary: Two music beds for the canyon waves and the Matriarch over the radio, 28 lines from KSTR's announcer for the canyon news and your next goal, and the Dropship's engines, all made with ElevenLabs.

entry.title: The balance pass: about ×2 the mining curve, never over ×2.5
entry.summary: Missions and canyon waves paid far too well. Measured against the pace model and cut: a pilot who does everything now runs ×1.86 to ×2.02 the mining curve, and level 10 takes 36 minutes.

entry.title: Two more canyons: the brine and the roost
entry.summary: The Drowned Cut in Brine Pans, where the Brood's walkers wade at half speed, and The Roost in Dust Terraces, where every Gloamwing comes off a spire over the walls.

entry.title: By day you see the whole region
entry.summary: No fog by day: every unit, bug and building in your region is sent and drawn, and dusk eases the sight down to the night's. Measured at the nest and at The Fork.

entry.title: Frontier pilots: you're no longer the only one out here
entry.summary: Five pilots of the server's own in every world, with callsigns, paints and habits, mining, building, fighting and talking on the radio by the same rules as you.

entry.title: The realm under siege: the M8 showreel
entry.summary: The M8 showreel: 67 seconds of the Brood, the Citadel's guns, the Dropship, The Fork and the Matriarch, cut the morning after I asked the agents for all of it.

entry.title: Holding The Fork: ten waves, and the Matriarch if you fail
entry.summary: The canyon game: ten waves of the Brood down The Fork's two arms, guns on the rims, and if a wave breaks through, the Matriarch comes out of the tunnel and fells every turret.

entry.title: The Dropship: no more flying alone
entry.summary: The Prospector no longer flies by itself. Pilots build Landing Pads and ride the Dropship between them: board, lift off, bank under the ringed giant, dash through cloud and land in another region, 16 to 20 seconds and never a fade.

entry.title: The Fork: the first canyon to hold
entry.summary: The first canyon: The Fork in Cold Fork, two winding arms from Brood tunnels to a prize of 36,000 ore and 6,000 MH, with 12 build spots on the rims for the turrets that will hold it.

entry.title: Valleys, not tiles: the regions reshaped
entry.summary: The nine regions reshaped as natural basins: bays, rock spurs, necks, islands of rock, terraced walls and passages that narrow like canyon mouths, with one high land of rock running between them.

entry.title: A quieter HUD: the same moments, before and after
entry.summary: The HUD, decluttered: one lane of toasts at the upper left, one banner slot under the compass, a contract panel a third of its old height, and the same moments before and after.

entry.title: “I reached level 10, now what?”
entry.summary: After the first ten minutes, KSTR now keeps one goal in front of every pilot, from a chain of 15 picked by level and by what the pilot has done, from pumping MH at level 3 to the Matriarch at 35.

entry.title: The Brood, painted: before and after the art pass
entry.summary: The art pass on the Brood: veined egg shells lit from within, opal chitin that shifts colour with the view, glass wings, the Matriarch's glowing sac and crown, and the gatling gun painted from its forge concept.

entry.title: Through the walls: walking between regions
entry.summary: Each region now has a ground of its own, cliff walls and passages, and walking from one region into the next happens without a reload or a jump.

entry.title: The world map: the real ground, seen from above
entry.summary: Press M for a picture of every region you've been to, its real ground seen from above, with pilots, mercenaries, the Brood, buildings and deposits live on it and a tooltip on each.

entry.title: The Matriarch wakes in Slag Pockets
entry.summary: The Brood's queen now lives at her nest in Slag Pockets: 6,000 hp, a slam, an acid spit and a roar that rallies her horde. Pilots who fell her share 3,000 ore, 1,500 MH and a rare blueprint.

entry.title: Guns for the realm: the Citadel shoots back
entry.summary: Four corner turrets on every Citadel, a Sentinel AA tower and a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and upgrades on every turret paid from your own wallet.

entry.title: Mercenaries: they mine while you sleep
entry.summary: Hire mercenary prospectors at the Citadel: in a world day each one mines what you mine in an hour, and they keep working while the game is closed.

entry.title: The world runs on after you quit
entry.summary: Quit the game and the world keeps going: the local server stays up, the clock turns, meteors fall and the Brood roams, at about 0.008% of a CPU core.

entry.title: Coming next: guns for the realm, and a canyon to hold
entry.summary: Coming, not in the game yet: the Citadel's guns, an AA tower, a gatling gun firing red-hot ore-and-MH rounds, and a canyon the pilots defend wave by wave.

entry.title: The Brood: from a painting to the world in a day
entry.summary: The first enemies: four alien bugs, from concept paintings to blockout models to the world, where they linger at deposits, bite, dive, eat ore and raid buildings.

entry.title: Missions, the Journal and three voices
entry.summary: The Citadel offers missions in three tiers, a Journal keeps them, and three narrators read every briefing.

entry.title: The realm: shared buildings, a tax and a shop
entry.summary: Every building now belongs to every pilot. The Citadel takes 10% of each unload into a realm wallet and sells blueprints and supplies.

entry.title: How we got here
entry.summary: Two days, seven milestones of the MMORPG mode: our own server, a world that lasts, a hundred levels, the ringshadow sweep and starfall.
